card: Enforces explicit range checking on numeric configuration arguments instead of allowing negative or out-of-range values to silently wrap, overflow, or invert time offsets. Options validated include -dbbatchsize, -maxtipage, mempool cluster limits, buffer sizes, timeouts, and wallet confirmation targets. The author notes that a negative -dbbatchsize wrapped to an immense unsigned integer and disabled database flushing during reindex, while an out-of-range -txconfirmtarget silently forced all wallet transactions onto fallback fees.
changed_since_previous: The scope and validated configuration arguments remain the same as in the previous description, with minor refinements to range bounds and test coverage.
evidence: PR description and commit 0ad0c71387: 'A negative -dbbatchsize wrapped to a huge value and disabled batch flushing, so a reindex could hold an unbounded batch in memory.'
Source comments in src/node/chainstatemanager_args.cpp: 'A negative max tip age would put the IBD cutoff in the future, so the node would never consider its tip recent and would stay in IBD.'

Source comments and functional tests in test/functional/wallet_fallbackfee.py: 'A confirmation target above what the fee estimator tracks would make every transaction fall back to -fallbackfee, so it is rejected instead of being silently accepted.'
Source comments in src/node/mempool_args.cpp: 'A negative expiry would move the expiration cutoff into the future, and a huge one would overflow the hours-to-seconds conversion.'
problem: Numeric arguments were read as signed integers without bounds validation before being cast to narrower or unsigned internal types. Passing negative or out-of-range values caused silent integer wrap-around, overflows, or logic inversion: negative -dbbatchsize disabled database batch flushes during reindex, negative -maxtipage kept nodes permanently stuck in initial block download, negative -datacarriersize permitted unlimited OP_RETURN sizes, and out-of-range -txconfirmtarget caused all wallet transactions to silently fall back to -fallbackfee.

risk.why: Incorrect range validation or off-by-one errors could cause existing user configuration files to fail to start bitcoind or misconfigure mempool and wallet policies.

scope_notes: Touches option parsing across several subsystems (init, chainstate, mempool, wallet, net). Most of the diff consists of unit and functional tests covering boundary and error cases.
summary: Enforces bounds checking on numeric configuration options across node startup, chainstate, mempool, networking, and wallet initialization. Options that previously accepted negative or out-of-range values—including -dbbatchsize, -dbcrashratio, -maxtipage, -limitclustersize, -limitclustercount, -mempoolexpiry, -datacarriersize, buffer limits, -timeout, and -txconfirmtarget—now raise fatal initialization errors instead of wrapping into unsigned types, inverting time calculations, or silently falling back to defaults. The change also marks numeric options as non-negatable and adds =<n> placeholders to their -help text.
